workflow has no "concurrency:", so every run of it executes at the same time even when a newer run supersedes the older ones. add a top-level "concurrency:" with a "group:" and "cancel-in-progress: true"

trigger "workflow_run" is dangerous: it runs in the context of the default branch with a write token and secrets, but processes artifacts and metadata produced by a run that a fork may control. consider a reusable workflow called with "workflow_call" instead, and never trust the artifacts or the event payload

"pull-requests: write" lets the job create and modify pull requests, comments and reviews, and the workflow runs on "workflow_run" which people without write access can trigger. check that the job needs it and cannot run untrusted code
